prose: Continuous dispatch across four kilometers of copper pneumatic tubing wore 3.8mm off the forward wool-felt sealing gasket. The resulting high-pressure air blow-by reduced capsule transit speed from 14 m/s down to 6 m/s, causing transit timeout alarms.

Failure of the terminal dashpot air cushion valve allowed a 110mm carrier to slam into the receiving hopper at 16 m/s. The severe deceleration impact split the red vulcanized fiber cylinder along its seam, scattering written intelligence dispatches.

Rotating the brass collar index ring on the capsule body aligned electrical contact pins for Sub-Level 4. As the canister sped past optical-magnetic track sensors, the circuit closed, energizing solenoid diverters to switch the carrier into the hospital siding.

Overloading the carrier with 3.2 kg of crushed lead-ore drill core exceeded the pneumatic lifting pressure gradient. The sluggish canister stalled inside a 90-degree long-radius bend, blocking the main inter-vault dispatch trunk line for twelve hours.

Desiccation of the flared steer-hide leather sealing skirt left the leather stiff and brittle. The un-oiled skirt failed to expand against the brass tube walls under 0.6 bar driving pressure, stranding the carrier halfway through the ventilation duct run.

Milling a resonant acoustic whistle port into the aluminum head cap produced a sharp 2.4 kHz piercing tone propelled by bypass airflow. The acoustic arrival signal alerted bunker dispatchers ten seconds before the capsule docked in the drop tray.

Embedding an axial neodymium ring magnet in the carrier nose pulsed external inductive pick-up coils strapped around the brass conduit. The central dispatcher board tracked the capsule's position across forty-two junction checkpoints in real time.

Molding deep concentric corrugations into the synthetic buna rubber nose cone absorbed 95% of kinetic energy upon high-speed terminal arrival. Vials of liquid biological culture transported inside survived 18 m/s impacts without hairline glass fractures.
